pages.title: Getting started
pages.text: Getting started This wiki is made of two GitHub repositories, so editors can change pages without ever touching the site's code. Repository Holds Who can write The site (app) repo The editor and page layout Maintainers only The content repo The pages and images Maintainers and editors Becoming an editor Ask a maintainer to add you as a collaborator on the content repository (Write access). On GitHub, create a fine-grained token limited to that repository with Contents and Pull requests set to read & write. Open the wiki, press Edit, then Save, and paste the token when asked. It stays in your browser. Not an editor yet? Anyone with a GitHub account can still suggest a change. Create a classic token with the public_repo scope and your edit is sent as a pull request for a maintainer to review. Good to know Pages usually appear to everyone within a few minutes of saving. You see your own change immediately. Every change is kept in the content repository's history, so mistakes can always be undone. Maintainers can set "directCommit": false in config.json so that all edits go through pull requests. Back to Welcome.

pages.title: How to edit pages
pages.text: How to edit pages Click ✎ Edit at the top right (or press E). Everything on the page becomes editable, and nothing is saved until you press Save. Writing blocks Every paragraph, heading, list item, and picture is a block. Hover a block to see its handles on the left: + adds a new block below ⋮⋮ opens a menu to turn it into something else, duplicate it, or delete it — drag it to move it Type / on an empty line to open the command menu and pick a block type. Shortcuts that save time You type You get # , ## , ### Headings - or Bulleted list 1. Numbered list [] To-do list > Quote --- then Enter Divider [[ Link to another page Select any text to get the formatting bar: bold, italic, strikethrough, code, and links. Tab and Shift+Tab indent list items. Examples Click the icon on a callout to cycle through Note, Tip, Important, Warning and Caution. Learn the slash menu Link to a page with [[ Try nesting this item with Tab // Code blocks keep their formatting const greet = (name) => Hello, ${name}!; Saving When you press Save, you will be asked to sign in with a GitHub token the first time. Then either your change goes live right away, or it is sent as a pull request — whichever your permissions allow. See Getting started for the details.

pages.title: Welcome
pages.text: Welcome to the wiki This is a shared knowledge base that anyone on the team can improve. Pages are stored as plain Markdown files in a GitHub repository, but you never have to touch Markdown — just click Edit and write, like in Notion. Press Ctrl K (or ⌘ K) to search every page, or type inside a page to link to another one. Where to start [[How to edit pages — a two-minute tour of the editor Getting started — setting up and publishing your own copy of this wiki Team handbook — an example of nested pages Style guide — keeping pages consistent Why a wiki? Good notes stay useful when they are easy to find, easy to link, and easy to fix. Every page here keeps its full history in Git, so nothing is ever lost, and edits from people without write access arrive as pull requests that can be reviewed first. Who can edit? Anyone with a GitHub account. People with write access to the repository publish straight away; everyone else sends their edit as a pull request.

pages.title: Style guide
pages.text: Style guide Small habits that keep a shared wiki pleasant to read. Titles and structure Name pages for what people will search for, not for how you think about them. Start with one sentence that says what the page is for. Use headings freely — the outline on the right is built from them. Linking Link generously with Page title. A red dashed link means the page doesn't exist yet; click it to create it. Pages that link here appear under Linked from at the bottom of each page, so you never need to maintain "see also" lists by hand. Keep it tidy Never paste passwords, tokens, or private customer data into a page. The repository history keeps everything. See also Team handbook and How to edit pages.
